To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flexural strength and stiffness of reinforced concrete beams with recycled aggregate are comparable to that of companion beams with virgin aggregate, and the recycled concrete is suitable for reinforced concrete structures.

the flexural behavior and the ultimate flexural strength of recycled concrete beams can be predicted with a good accuracy by using the same mechanics as those for concrete with virgin aggregate, and that the recycled concrete can be applied for reinforced concrete structures as long as the design and construction are carried out with proper care.

the flexural behavior, including the strength and the ductility, of reinforced recycled concrete beam can be predicted based on the mechanics of reinforced concrete beam with virgin aggregate concrete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties and the behavior of concrete with recycled aggregate.

the following issues: (1) The properties of recycled aggregate concrete, (2) The flexural behavior of recycled concrete beams, (3) The flexural strength of recycled concrete members, and (4) The flexural design method of recycled concrete members.
the mechanical properties of recycled concrete as a function of recycled content and the flexural behavior under service load conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of recycled concrete in reinforced concrete members can be considered for structures where the design is based on the flexural behavior and where the tension reinforcement ratio is relatively small.

the recycled concrete is applicable to reinforced concrete structures as long as the following conditions are met: (i) recycled coarse aggregates are used, (ii) the recycled concrete has a compressive strength not less than 30MPa, (iii) the recycled concrete is not used in a structural element that is subjected to a tensile stress, and (iv) the recycled concrete does not have a significant amount of recycled fine aggregates.
recycled concrete is a feasible material for structural concrete applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the flexural behavior and strength of reinforced concrete beams with recycled aggregate are similar to those of companion virgin concrete specimens, provided that the recycled aggregate is used with the proper combination of recycled coarse aggregate and recycled fine aggregate.

the recycled aggregate concrete is not inferior to the virgin aggregate concrete in terms of the flexural behavior and that the flexural strength of reinforced recycled concrete beam is comparable to that of reinforced virgin concrete beam under the proper design.

concrete made with 50 % of recycled aggregate could be used for the flexural members of reinforced concrete structures, provided that the recycled aggregate is produced mainly from reinforced concrete members, the water to binder ratio is not higher than 0.5, and the concrete is properly cured.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of recycled aggregate in concrete does not necessarily lead to inferior structural performance.
the recycled concrete has a potential for structural application as long as the design and construction are properly carried out.
it is possible to utilize recycled concrete for concrete structures, if the design is properly done.
